title: Telling the Story of the Data

steps.body: Data tells a story: who got the most, who got the fewest, how many in all. True sentences match the counts.
steps.narration: Data tells a story: who got the most, who got the fewest, how many in all. True sentences match the counts.

widget.prompt: The story starts here: how many votes does this tally row for Cats show? Move the marker.

commonResults.feedback: That reads only the crossed five-group. Three single marks follow it: 6, 7, 8.
That counts only the singles and skips the five-group entirely.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Count what is actually drawn — fives for each crossed group, then ones for the singles — and move the marker to that number.
widget.successFeedback: One five-group and three singles — 8 votes. Now the story about Cats can be checked.

predict.prompt: A classmate says “Cats got the most votes”. How do you check the claim?

options.label: See which row is listed first

predict.reveal: Claims about data are checked against the counts, not confidence or position. The biggest count decides “most.”

widget.prompt: Votes: Cats 8, Dogs 5, Fish 3. Which sentence tells the data's story truthfully?

options.label: Cats got the most votes
options.feedback: Correct — 8 is the biggest count, so that sentence matches the data.

options.label: Fish got the most votes
options.feedback: Fish got 3 votes — the SMALLEST count. The data says the opposite.

options.label: Every category got the same votes
options.feedback: The three counts are all different, so no two categories tied.

options.label: Cats got the fewest votes
options.feedback: Cats has the biggest count, 8. It got the most, not the fewest.
